metric_rationale: This is signed top-cue endorsement: +1 when the subject follows the uniquely highest-validity cue and -1 when they override it. It uses all 96 trials, including mirrored A/B versions, so response-side tendencies cancel and each subject's estimate is relatively precise. Take The Best predicts a positive score at every evidence level because the first cue always discriminates. Tallying predicts zero contribution on the two tally-tie conditions and negative contributions on the ten conditions where the accumulating lower cues defeat the top-cue winner. Thus the theories place the metric on opposite sides of zero, producing a larger and more stable separation than a slope based on only a subset of evidence levels.

This is a signed high-validity-cue alignment score: +1 when a choice follows the first discriminating cue in validity order and -1 when it opposes that cue. Because every designed pair has an equal tally, Tallying predicts independent guessing and hence an expected score of 0. Take The Best predicts the first discriminating cue's option, producing an expected score of (1-epsilon)*tanh(beta/2), which is positive for every allowed parameter combination. Pooling all 96 trials gives a low-noise within-subject estimate, while the option-swapped mirrors ensure that generic A/B response bias cannot create a positive score. The metric tests a behavioral covariance between choices and cue rank rather than merely overall choice proportions.

This is a preregistered configuration-sensitivity covariance after orienting every stimulus toward its 3-cue tally winner. The centered weight is the majority-choice probability predicted by a fixed midpoint instantiation of Accessibility-Balanced Evidence Integration. Thus configurations where the majority coalition occupies strong late cues receive positive weights, while configurations where its three cues are outweighed by two late cues receive negative weights. Under Tallying, every oriented trial has the identical 3-versus-2 margin and hence the same expected majority-choice rate; centering the weights makes its expected metric exactly zero for every beta and epsilon. The advocated theory predicts that observed majority choice covaries strongly with these weights. All 96 responses contribute to the scalar, mirror trials are automatically placed in the same canonical orientation, and the balanced repeated schedule keeps the per-subject estimate comparatively stable. The weights are fixed independently of responses rather than fitted to the observed data.

This is an accessibility-weighted rate of choosing the option supported by the later of the two discriminating experts. It recodes the mirrored A/B trials into a common direction, thereby cancelling response-side preference, and pools all repetitions so it remains stable at the individual-subject level. Tallying gives every trial an exact 0.5 probability because each option wins one cue. Accessibility-Balanced Integration instead predicts increasingly frequent selection of the later-supported option as its supporting cue moves farther down the display. The exponential contrast weight is a matched-filter approximation based on the midpoint of the competing theory's recency-gradient range: it downweights the weak, noisy nearest-position contrast and emphasizes trials on which the competing theory predicts its largest departure from chance.

This is the proportion of choices favoring the option with greater exponentially recency-weighted cue support. In every designed conflict, that option is the adjacent late-cue coalition rather than the coalition supplying the final discriminating cue. Accessibility-Balanced Evidence Integration therefore predicts values above 0.5, whereas Switch-Closure Coalition Integration predicts values below 0.5 because its balanced-coalition closure gate favors the opposite option. The six exact A/B mirrors make the measure insensitive to a stable A-versus-B response bias. Averaging all 96 binary observations gives a stable per-subject estimate, while the fixed midpoint recency gradient avoids estimating noisy subject-level parameters.

The metric measures the theories' clearest opposing qualitative prediction while remaining response-side invariant. For every trial it identifies the option supported by Experts 1–3, pools all 96 mirrored and repeated trials within each subject, and asks whether that option wins a majority of the subject's choices. Switch-Closure Coalition Integration predicts majority support for this early coherent three-cue coalition; Accessibility-Balanced Evidence Integration predicts majority opposition because its later two-cue coalition receives greater accessibility weight. Averaging a subject-level majority indicator sharply reduces trial-level choice noise, while the exact A/B mirrors prevent a generic preference for response A or B from producing the effect.

This metric is the weighted difference in endorsement of the three-cue coalition between entry-compact configurations ([adjacent cue, then gap]) and their exit-compact counterparts ([gap, then adjacent cue]). It recodes choices relative to the three-cue coalition, so the exact A/B mirrors cancel response-side bias. It also contrasts configurations within the same 3-versus-2 coalition sizes, cue validities, onset, and number of adjacent links, removing stable subject differences in overall preference for larger coalitions. Reliability-Compressed Parsing Mixtures predicts a positive contrast for every integration style, with a larger effect at wider gaps; the bounded gap weight emphasizes those more diagnostic trials while retaining all 96 observations. Switch-Closure Coalition Integration assigns matched entry- and exit-compact configurations the same structural gate because their onset and adjacency coherence are identical, predicting a contrast near zero.

This is the within-subject early-versus-late change in endorsement of the three-cue coalition, coded independently of whether that coalition is displayed as A or B. Switch-Closure Coalition Integration predicts a positive contrast because its amplified near-balance gate favors the three-cue coalition when it begins before the two-cue coalition and disfavors it when it begins afterward. Reliability-Compressed Parsing Mixtures predicts the same three-cue endorsement rate in both groups: coalition sizes and internal gap patterns are fixed, and its relevant parsing descriptor is translation-invariant. Averaging 48 observations on each side uses every trial, while the within-subject difference cancels stable integration-style effects, general preference for three versus two cues, and response-side tendencies; the mirrored pairs further balance A/B assignment.

This is the proportion of choices favoring the coalition supported by the final discriminating cue, coded independently of response side. Exact A/B mirrors therefore cancel generic A-versus-B bias, while all 96 observations contribute to a stable subject-level estimate. Reliability-Compressed Parsing Mixtures predicts a population-common completion increment and hence a closure-choice rate clearly above 0.5. Exchangeable Corroboration has no completion term: its stable cue-salience profiles can generate individual closure preferences, but exchangeability makes those effects population-centered at 0.5. The metric directly tests the design's common directional prediction without relying on a deterministic or definitional consequence of the advocated theory.

This is the composition-load-weighted probability of choosing the equal-validity coalition, coded identically across the A/B mirror trials. Weighting by the absolute difference in pairwise diagnostic-strength products emphasizes the high-validity conditions where the theories diverge most, while retaining all six conditions to reduce trial noise and average over cue-specific salience. The advocated theory's redundancy discount predicts a value substantially below 0.5, especially for the strongest equal-validity pairs. The competing theory has no composition discount in these separated 2-versus-2 displays and predicts a value near 0.5 or slightly above it due to reliability weighting. Mirror-invariant coding cancels response-side tendencies, and the weighted proportion remains well-defined for both pooled data and individual-subject slices.

This is the within-subject increase in choosing the variable target coalition when its reliability gap crosses from the narrow-overlap region (gaps 0.00 and 0.04) to the heterogeneous region (0.10 and 0.18). It codes choices relative to the target coalition, so A/B mirroring cancels response-side bias. Reliability-Schema Source Inference predicts a pronounced step because inferred source overlap falls sharply at the larger gaps, whereas Exchangeable Corroboration predicts only a small change in its smooth composition load. Pooling two gap levels on each side uses all 96 trials and yields a lower-variance subject estimate than an endpoint-only contrast.

This is the subject-balanced probability of choosing a distributed-validity coalition, with the two A/B presentation roles weighted equally. Exchangeable Corroboration approximately equates clustered and distributed triples because their size, summed bounded strength, and mean pairwise composition load are matched, predicting a value near 0.5 after crossed-coalition averaging. Reliability-Schema Source Inference discounts the exact 0.87 pair inside each clustered triple and therefore predicts a visibly higher value. Averaging all 96 repetitions and exact mirrors suppresses binomial noise, response-side bias, and much of the advocated theory's exchangeable cue-specific salience variation.

Mirror-corrected distributed-coalition preference, scaled from -1 (always chooses the clustered triple) to +1 (always chooses the distributed triple), with 0 denoting indifference. Equal weighting of the eight configurations removes response-side and cell-frequency effects. The advocated theory predicts a consistently positive contrast because both its within-coalition compression and relational topology operation favor each distributed triple. The competing theory lacks that common topology term; the matched composition loads and crossed coalition identities leave its population contrast near zero, while repeated trials and averaging across all four crossings suppress choice noise and idiosyncratic cue-salience effects.

The metric is the choice rate for the more reliability-distributed coalition, restricted to the zero-versus-wide endpoint comparison and the first three gap increments. Contextual Reliability-Region Compression predicts its strongest and most consistent release from duplicate-pair compression on exactly these comparisons, while the two widest-gap adjacent comparisons should contribute mostly noise and are omitted. Exchangeable Corroboration lacks a reliability-gap operation, and the design equates coalition size and order-free composition statistics, so its population prediction remains near 0.5. Pooling four mirrored comparison types provides 64 observations per subject, reducing binomial variance, while A/B mirroring cancels response-side bias. Classification is stimulus-based and therefore remains valid under randomized trial order.

This is the preregistered coalition-size interaction: separated-coalition choice probability in 3-versus-3 contests minus the same probability in 2-versus-2 contests. It codes choices relative to coalition type rather than A/B side, so the exact mirrors cancel response-side bias and stable cue-specific salience. Contextual Reliability-Region Compression predicts a positive onset because its duplicate-pair topology operation is activated only once an outsider creates a triad. Reliability-Space Credit Sharing penalizes the equal-validity pair already in dyads and therefore predicts little or negative change after the outsider is added. Each subject contributes 48 observations to each term, making the contrast relatively stable while directly targeting the theories' cardinality-specific disagreement.

This is the mirror-corrected selection rate for the single-duplicate coalitions (the coalitions supported by cues 8–15) against the double-duplicate coalitions (cues 0–7). Reliability-Space Credit Sharing discounts all four members of a double-duplicate coalition but only the duplicated 0.75 pair in a single-duplicate coalition, so it predicts a substantial preference for the latter. Contextual Reliability-Region Compression largely equates these coalitions because their composition load and duplicate-pair-in-context topology are matched, predicting a value much nearer 0.5. Equal weighting of the A-side and B-side mirror orientations removes response-side bias, while pooling all 96 repeated choices keeps the per-subject estimate comparatively stable. The measure is a direct, non-tautological behavioral contrast rather than a restatement of either model's internal calculation.

This metric targets the full predicted cardinality profile rather than only the dyad-to-triad slope. It recodes every response as choosing the reliability-diverse rather than duplicate-containing coalition, thereby combining the exact A/B mirrors and suppressing response-side bias. Categorical Source-Budget Inference predicts relatively reduced diverse preference in dyads, enhanced preference in triads when only the diverse coalition crosses the two-to-three-source release, and reduced preference again in tetrads. Reliability-Space Credit Sharing instead predicts especially strong diverse preference in dyads followed by a smoother decline. Thus the theories differ with signs approximately negative, positive, and negative for advocated-minus-competing choice rates at cardinalities 2, 3, and 4. The weights (-1, 0.53, -0.51) align all three differences in one direction and approximately inverse-variance weight their expected binomial contrasts. Each component uses 32 responses per subject, including both mirror orientations, so the statistic remains defined and comparatively stable on individual-subject slices.

This is the mirror-corrected chain-coalition choice rate, with equal weight assigned to each of the four crossed chain/comparison configurations and then to each subject. It targets the design's sign-reversing prediction: Reliability-Space Credit Sharing predicts selection of the five-member reliability chain above chance because its mostly nonoverlapping members retain independent credit, whereas Categorical Source-Budget Inference predicts selection below chance because the chain collapses transitively to one source while the comparison coalition receives three source budgets. Coding choices relative to the chain rather than as raw A/B responses removes response-side bias. Averaging all 96 trials and balancing the four configurations should also yield substantially lower between-subject noise than a statistic based on individual trial types.

This is the mirror-corrected wide-minus-narrow target-choice slope. Each response is recoded as choosing the target coalition, irrespective of whether that coalition appeared as A or B, and then averaged over all target identities, reference identities, mirrors, and repetitions. Tagged Partial-Independence Coalition Coding places both 0.0030 and 0.0058 target dyads inside the same duplicate tag and gives them the same ordinal diversity, so it predicts a slope near zero. Reliability-Space Credit Sharing predicts a substantially positive slope because overlap—and hence redundancy—falls sharply between these two separations. Pooling 48 observations in each gap condition per subject keeps trial-level variance low, while mirror recoding removes choice-side effects.

Mirror-corrected probability of choosing the locally spaced chain coalition over the coalition containing two exact-duplicate pairs. The advocated reliability-space theory predicts a strong chain preference because exact duplicates receive much more overlapping credit than the spaced chain members. The tagged theory assigns both coalition types approximately two duplicate-credit groups and therefore predicts a value near 0.5. All 96 trials contribute, while separately averaging chain-on-A and chain-on-B trials removes response-side bias and yields a stable within-subject estimate.

The metric is the prevalence of subjects who choose the reliability-diverse coalition on at least two thirds of the 96 trials. Diverse choice is coded relative to the stimulus, so exact A/B mirrors remove response-side bias, while crossing both diverse and both duplicate blocks averages over coalition identity. Tagged Partial-Independence Coalition Coding predicts diverse-choice rates around 0.76–0.90, making the supermajority criterion likely for nearly every subject. Opponent-Relative Stratified Sampling instead pools these large one-sided duplicate contrasts and predicts rates near 0.50, making a 2/3 rate very unlikely over 96 observations. The subject-level threshold converts the predicted separation into a low-variance prevalence contrast while remaining an empirically falsifiable behavioral endpoint rather than a direct restatement of either model's computations.

The metric is the mirror-corrected proportion of choices favoring a 0.598/0.602 near-duplicate dyad over a 0.600/0.600 exact-duplicate dyad. It pools all 96 trials, including every coalition crossing and both A/B orientations, so stable cue-specific preferences and response-side bias are averaged out. Opponent-Relative Stratified Sampling predicts a substantial preference for the near-duplicate coalition because only the exact dyad incurs the strong opponent-relative concentration vulnerability. Tagged Partial-Independence Coding assigns both dyads the same duplicate multiplicity and nearly identical evidence, predicting a proportion near 0.5. The statistic is also well-defined per subject and benefits from all 96 repeated observations, keeping between-subject sampling variance low.

This is the mirror-corrected separated-coalition preference, coded from -1 (always choose a paired-endpoint coalition) to +1 (always choose a fully separated coalition), with 0 denoting no topology preference. It uses all 96 observations per subject and pools the four exact A/B mirrors, thereby cancelling stable response-side bias and reducing binomial noise. Tagged Partial-Independence Coalition Coding assigns the paired and separated tetrads the same duplicate multiplicity, nominal size, and ordinal diversity, so it predicts a value near zero. Adaptive Source-Resolution Compression treats every positive reliability gap as individuation evidence but treats exact equality as dependence evidence, so it predicts a positive value. The contrast targets a substantive topology preference rather than generic choice stochasticity or reliability weighting.

This is the preregistered mirror-corrected probability of choosing the broad-gap dyad over the narrow-gap dyad. It directly targets the design's intended qualitative disagreement rather than an indirect coverage gradient. Tagged Partial-Independence Coalition Coding necessarily places the two members of each 0.004 narrow dyad in one duplicate-credit group but keeps both members of each 0.014 broad dyad separate, predicting a substantial broad-dyad advantage. Adaptive Source-Resolution Compression treats both nonzero gaps primarily as evidence for two individuated sources, predicting a rate much closer to 0.5. All 96 trials contribute to the estimate, and separately averaging trials where the broad coalition is A versus B removes stable response-side bias. The statistic therefore has low binomial variance within subjects while preserving the theories' large predicted mean difference. It is not trivially true under the advocated theory: it is an empirical choice proportion whose near-chance prediction follows from the theory's continuous source-individuation mechanism.

This is the prevalence of subjects whose mirror-corrected choices show a majority preference for the dispersed coalition. Compact-coalition choices are averaged separately when compact is A and when compact is B, then those rates are equally averaged, eliminating stable response-side bias. The advocated theory predicts a robust dispersed majority because four singleton credit accounts dominate the duplicate-tagged compact coalition; the competitor predicts the reverse because the compact, replicated reliability strata are more coherent. Thresholding each subject's estimate after aggregating all 96 trials converts this sign-reversing prediction into a stable subject-level classification, reducing sensitivity to binomial choice noise and idiosyncratic cue salience while remaining entirely response-dependent.

This is the side-invariant compact-coalition choice rate on the 64 repeated trials comparing a replicated compact tetrad with the two clearly diffuse chains (adjacent gaps .014 and .020). These conditions target the theories' strongest structural disagreement while pooling two chain identities, two compact identities, exact A/B mirrors, and eight repetitions to limit cue-salience, side-bias, and binomial variance. Coherence-Constrained Reliability-Strata Inference predicts that supported compact strata are protected from dispersion and should outperform these unsupported reliability chains. Tagged Partial-Independence Coalition Coding instead splits both diffuse chains into four singleton duplicate groups, allowing them substantially more accumulated credit than the compact tetrad. Excluding the less diagnostic .008 chain avoids dilution from subjects whose duplicate tolerance or clustering width places that chain near a grouping boundary.
